Maya (PM): Quick thread Customers keep pushing for an onprem upgrade flow that they can run themselves with minimal Redwood involvement. They want a dry-run, clear rollback, and option to keep control-plane read-only for a window. Need tech tradeoffs + launch gates.

Ravi (Eng): Sounds good. My high-level split: MVP = preflight + dry-run report + rolling drain + scripted rollback. Optional = control-plane tunnel, signed offline installer workflow, advanced net-pol mapping.

Noah (NetOps): Network concerns: many customers sit behind NAT or use overlay networks. Preflight must detect: external IP NAT, overlapping CIDRs across clusters, and blocked egress/proxy rules. It should produce mitigation suggestions, not just fail.

Jill (Security): Must include: installer signature verification (offline), KMS key presence check in preflight, and audit-event emission for upgrade actions. Threat model for the upgrade path is required before beta.

Tori (CustSuccess): Example ask: MediCore wants a 72h read-only control-plane window post-upgrade and the ability to trigger rollback locally without us. Also they need a compliance-ready dry-run PDF.

Ravi (Eng): Proposed UX: redwoodctl upgrade plan --cluster ./cluster.yaml --dry-run --report ./upgrade-report.json --read-only-window 72h
Report will include: ordered migration steps, expected downtime per service, required ports/IPs, risk flags (CIDR overlap, blocked port), and rollback commands.

Noah (NetOps): For overlapping IPs we can propose namespace-scoped port remaps and a suggested NAT translation table in the report. Also the preflight should probe egress to our artifact URLs (and detect corporate proxies).

Maya (PM): Launch gates (MVP): 1) preflight + report; 2) rolling upgrade with migrate.lock + concurrency defaults; 3) rollback script tested in 2 customers (one VPC, one airgapped); 4) docs & playbook for NetOps. Anything else?

Jill (Security): Add: offline signature verification test in trials and audit logs stored locally with ability to export. Also ensure the migrate.lock can't be abused to deadlock cluster.

Ravi (Eng): Implementation notes: add migrate.lock in control-plane state; upgrade run emits trace_id and stores run metadata to /var/lib/redwood/upgrade_runs/<trace_id>. For read-only window we flip control-plane to read-only mode (API returns 423 for mutating calls). Escape hatch = redwoodctl upgrade abort --trace <id> which triggers graceful agent uninstall + handover.

Tori (CustSuccess): I'll prepare the compliance dry-run template. Need the CLI flags finalized and the sample report fields.

Noah (NetOps): Edge case: customers with strict egress can't use our artifact URLs. Support an offline-image-diff report: installer includes checksums and we provide a minimal diff tool that runs locally. Stretch but valuable for airgapped.

Ravi (Eng): Estimates: preflight + dry-run report + report generator = 3-4 dev-weeks. migrate.lock + rolling drain + rollback = 3-4 dev-weeks. Signing + KMS integration + audit logs = 2-3 dev-weeks (security sprint). QA: 2 weeks with two customer trials.

Maya (PM): OK. Prioritize MVP for Q2 triage. Stretch items (BGP, zero-downtime KV migration, full tunnel option) scheduled Q3.

build-bot: CI: onprem/installer v0.36.2 build 2148801789 SUCCESS artifacts: s3://redwood-builds/onprem/v0.36.2/install.tar.gz

Jill (Security): I'll start the threat-model template and add signature verification tests to QA checklist.

Ravi (Eng): I'll open epics and draft the preflight schema. Will include sample report JSON schema.

Tori (CustSuccess): I'll reach out to MediCore to offer them the first dry-run slot.

Maya (PM): Thanks everyone. Action items: Ravi: RFC + epics; Noah: preflight net probe scenarios; Jill: threat model; Tori: trial POC. Schedule WG review next Tue.
